about.booking_terms: The rules a customer books a time or a stay with you on.
about.shop_terms: The rules of buying in your shop: the order, delivery, returns.

MarketingConsents.title: Marketing consents
MarketingConsents.description: Customers who agreed to receive the company's offers and promotions. The list comes from the consent journal: when, on which form and to which words the customer agreed. Nothing is edited here — a withdrawal is written as the journal's next line.
MarketingConsents.noAccess: The list of consents is read by the people who run the company.
MarketingConsents.caption: Customers' marketing consents
MarketingConsents.wordingUnknown: Words not recorded — this consent was written down before the journal kept its words, and the sentence of that day can no longer be read back (the company changed its name or the consent's sentence changed). The date and the form are certain.
MarketingConsents.empty: Nobody has agreed yet. The list fills up once customers tick the consent to offers and promotions on the booking form.
MarketingConsents.removedNote: Customers whose data was removed are not listed — nobody is left to write to. Their lines in the consent journal stay.
MarketingConsents.withdrawTitle: Write down that {name} withdraws the consent?
MarketingConsents.withdrawHint: The consent journal will say that the customer no longer wants offers and promotions — with today's date; the change history shows who wrote it down. The line cannot be removed. The earlier consent stays in the journal as evidence, and the customer may agree again with their next booking.
MarketingConsents.withdrawn: Written down: {name} no longer wants offers and promotions.
MarketingConsents.changed: This consent changed meanwhile — the list shows where it stands now.
MarketingConsents.withdrawFailed: Could not save the withdrawal. Try again.
MarketingConsents.loadError: The list of consents could not be loaded.

CustomerRemoval.pageDescription: When a customer asks for their data to be removed: find them by name, e-mail or phone and remove their data from the company's records. A removal cannot be undone — before you confirm, you see what stays and until when.
CustomerRemoval.noAccess: Customers' data is removed by the people who manage the company's bookings.
CustomerRemoval.searchLabel: The customer's name, e-mail or phone
CustomerRemoval.hint: Type at least two characters. We search among the customers you see in the calendar and in the orders — also those with no order at all.
CustomerRemoval.automatic: The company can also remove the data of customers with no recent visit by itself, after a time it chooses:
CustomerRemoval.caption: Customers found
CustomerRemoval.none: No customer matches “{q}”. A customer whose data was already removed cannot be found.
CustomerRemoval.more: Matching customers: {total}. Showing the first {shown} — type more to narrow it down.
CustomerRemoval.searchFailed: Could not search the customers. Try again.
CustomerRemoval.title: Remove the data of {name}?
CustomerRemoval.goes: This cannot be undone. What goes: the customer's name, e-mail and phone, their notes on visits, the address of a visit at theirs and the stored copies of messages to them; the customer's link for managing a booking stops working. It covers every visit and order of this customer.
CustomerRemoval.stays: What stays: dates, services, order numbers, lines and amounts — without the person's data — and the e-mails the customer already received.
CustomerRemoval.keptTitle: What else stays, and until when
CustomerRemoval.keptNothing: None of this customer's orders was paid for, so nothing that points at the person stays on the orders.
CustomerRemoval.previewFailed: Could not check what stays. Close the window and try again.
CustomerRemoval.failed: Could not remove the customer's data. Try again.

Orders.caption: The company's orders
Orders.searchHint: A part of an order's number, of the buyer's name or of their e-mail address
Orders.empty: No orders yet. They appear by themselves when a customer or the office books an offer that has a price.
Orders.emptyFiltered: No order matches the search and filters.
Orders.loadError: The orders could not be loaded.
Orders.permission: Orders are read by the company's owner, administrators and managers.
Orders.planTitle: The company's plan has no orders yet
Orders.plan: Orders are part of every current plan. A company on an earlier version of its plan gets them when it changes the plan.
Orders.planOwner: Orders are part of every current plan. A company on an earlier version of its plan gets them when it changes the plan — ask the company's owner.
Orders.orderLoadError: The order could not be loaded.
Orders.name: Name
Orders.buyerKept: The customer's data was removed on {date}. The buyer's details stay on this order until {until}: an order that was paid for is the company's sales record. After that day the system removes them by itself.
Orders.buyerRemoved: The customer's data was removed on {date}.
Orders.repriced: The amount changed when the booking got a new price. Before: {amounts}.
Orders.consentsCaption: The customer's consents with this order
Orders.noConsents: The customer accepted no document with this order.
Orders.refundOwed: To give back to the customer
Orders.noPayments: Nobody has marked a payment yet.
Orders.awaited: The order waits for a payment of {amount} by {date}. Once you mark it, the booking is confirmed. Without it by then the booking expires and the order is canceled.
Orders.balanceAwaited: The rest of the price, {amount}, is due by a transfer by {date}. The customer has the transfer details and will be reminded before the date.
Orders.balanceOverdue: The balance of {amount} was due by {date} and has not been marked. The booking stays confirmed, and the customer has been told. If the transfer arrived, mark the payment; calling the booking off is your own decision, in the calendar.
Orders.draftHint: This order waits for the company to answer the customer's booking request. It gets its number when the booking is accepted; until then it takes no payment.
Orders.recordHint: Write down what the customer paid at the desk or by transfer. Left to pay: {due}.
Orders.recordHintAwaited: The booking waits for a payment of {amount}. A payment of at least that confirms the booking; a smaller one is recorded and the rest stays awaited. Left to pay: {due}.
Orders.saveFailed: It could not be saved. Try again.
Orders.stale: Somebody changed this order in the meantime. We loaded it again — check the payments and try once more.
Orders.voidHint: Use this when a payment was marked by mistake. It stays in the order's history as taken back, and the order owes that amount again. This is not a refund to the customer.
Orders.noRefunds: Nobody has marked a refund yet.
Orders.refundOwedHint: To give back to the customer: {amount}. The amount follows the terms the booking was made under. Return it by a transfer or at the desk, then mark the refund.
Orders.refundHintOwed: Record what the company gave back to the customer. By the booking's terms {owed} is to be given back; the customer paid {paid}. A larger refund needs a reason. Saving moves no money — you return it yourself.
Orders.refundHint: Record what the company gave back to the customer. The customer paid {paid}. This refund does not follow from the order's terms, so give a reason. Saving moves no money — you return it yourself.
Orders.refundReasonHint: Shown on the order's page only. The customer does not get it.
Orders.refundReasonRequired: Give a reason for a refund beyond what the order's terms give back.
Orders.refundMail: The customer gets an e-mail with the amount and how it was given back — without the reason.
Orders.refundNoMail: The customer gave no e-mail address — let them know another way.
Orders.refundVoidHint: Use this when the refund was marked by mistake. It stays in the order's history as taken back, and the amount counts as paid for the order again.
Orders.refundVoidMail: The customer gets an e-mail saying the message about this refund was a mistake.
